column1: # LEVAIN — THE LANE OWNERSHIP MAP
# ⛔⛔ ONE LANE OWNS A FILE. A LANE MAY READ ANYTHING AND WRITE ONLY WHAT IT OWNS.
# ▶▶ THE PROTOCOL ITSELF LIVES IN FLOW, NOT HERE. Read
#    `~/Briefcase/flow/FLOW_DEV_PROTOCOL.md` → **`## Parallel Lanes — N agents, one repo`** for:
#    parallel-hands/serial-head and the `git reset --hard` discriminator · the gate on when NOT to
#    go parallel · the four-line commit protocol for a shared index · observation-vs-ruling and the
#    lane log · the two channels to the seat · the four cross-lane grant conditions ·
#    clean-worktree-for-anything-the-operator-grades · the LAUNCH and FAN-IN checklists · the
#    per-run kill criterion. Nothing generic is copied here; this file holds levain's own roster.
# ⛔ THIS FILE IS SEAT-OWNED. An ownership grant is a RULING. A lane asks; it does not edit.
# Ported from wisp's reference implementation 2026-09-03 (`tools/verify_lane.sh`,
# `tools/lane_brief.sh`, `tools/hooks/pre-commit`, `tools/install_hooks.sh`). levain had NO lane
# infrastructure before this date — every prior levain session was serial, which was correct while
# the work was serial and is not correct now that K4c and K1-part-2 are both live and independent.
# ── WHY THESE TWO LANES, AND WHY THE AXIS IS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE ─────────────────────────────────
#   The lane axis is FILE OWNERSHIP, MEASURED, not the mental module map. Verified on disk
#   2026-09-03 before drawing it, because the plan's claim that K4c and K1-part-2 "are independent"
#   is a claim about a symbol graph and had never been checked:
#   ⚠ THE NEAR-MISS. K1-part-2's prerequisite (`spore-438`, carry the drive mode in Conversation
#   state rather than the process-global `$LEVAIN_DRIVE_MODE`) looked like it must reach into
#   `levain/firing/confinement.py`, which is exactly where K4c adds its `bwrap` provider — and a
#   signature change crossing a seam two lanes share is 🔴 SERIAL-ONLY by construction, no matter
#   how small it looks. It does NOT reach there. `confinement.py` never reads the drive mode; it
#   names `drive.resolve_cred_floor` in comments and nothing else, and that function ALREADY takes
#   `mode=` as an explicit keyword (`levain/firing/drive.py`), so its four callers are
#   `session.py`, `cli.py`, `firing/openhands/tools.py` and `drive.py` — and none of them is
#   `confinement.py`. The seam is already parameterised, so the two lanes are genuinely disjoint.
#   ▶ RECORDED BECAUSE A NEGATIVE RESULT IS THE EXPENSIVE HALF: the next seat will have the same
#   worry, and re-deriving it costs the same four greps. If `resolve_cred_floor` ever grows a
#   session-carried form, THIS PARAGRAPH IS THE THING THAT GOES STALE — re-check it, do not cite it.
# ── THE KILL CRITERION IS PER-RUN AND LIVES AT THE LAUNCH, NOT HERE ──────────────────────────────
#   Registered by the seat at LAUNCH CHECKLIST step 5 and it DIES AT FAN-IN. An expired criterion is
#   the correct state between runs, not a gap to fill (`spore-413`: kill conditions are FELT, not
#   structured — this is the narrow bounded-protocol exception that ruling names).
# <lane-name>
# The SEAT owns everything not claimed by a lane below, and the seat is NEVER out of bounds
# (⚖ Phill 2026-08-27) — a seat commit outside its own rows is NAMED LOUDLY and is never fatal.
levain-seat
